title: Sub-gigabyte on-device LLM gains same-week Unsloth tuning support by Q3 2026
body: The release of Liquid AI's 230M-parameter LFM2.5 with launch-day llama.cpp, MLX, vLLM, SGLang and ONNX runtimes signals that a sub-gigabyte on-device model now ships against the full local-inference stack on day one. With Unsloth's v0.1.471-beta already landing first-class fine-tuning for frontier open weights within two days of release (GLM-5.2 on June 16, support on June 18), the same compression is coming to the edge tier. The prediction is that a sub-1B on-device model published this cycle will gain LoRA/QLoRA fine-tuning support in a mainstream tuning toolkit within the same week as its weights drop, closing the loop from open release to on-device customization. The forcing function is competitive: once one tuning library lands a popular edge checkpoint in days, the others must match the turnaround or cede the on-device developer audience.

reasoning.given: Unsloth landed GLM-5.2 fine-tuning two days after its June 16 open-weight release
reasoning.so_that: open-weight edge checkpoints get same-week tuning support, collapsing release-to-customization to days on-device
reasoning.landing: A sub-1B edge model gains same-week tuning support by Q3 2026
reasoning.plain_language: Tiny phone-sized AI models will become trainable just days after they are released.

summary: Liquid AI's 230M LFM2.5 ships launch-day across llama.cpp, MLX, vLLM, SGLang and ONNX, while Unsloth already adds frontier fine-tuning within two days of a release. Expect a sub-1B on-device model to gain same-week LoRA/QLoRA tuning support in a mainstream toolkit by Q3 2026.
